input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign — vLLM ROCm serving functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: whether vLLM serving on AMD
Instinct accelerators achieves functional and performance parity for the
platform's supported model set. It runs a validation campaign on physical AMD
Instinct hardware using upstream (unproductized) ROCm vLLM builds, and produces
the parity data plus the go/no-go scope that determines which models the
productized ROCm serving runtime will support. The platform currently ships
only CUDA runtime builds and has no first-hand ROCm parity data, so this
campaign is the gate for all serving productization work in this strategy.

## Scope

- Define the campaign methodology: per-model functional pass/fail criteria and
  performance parity measurement (relative to the existing CUDA runtime builds)
  for every model in the supported model set.
- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  coordination) — the access itself is externally controlled and tracked as a
  risk; the epic's deliverable is the validated data.
- Execute vLLM ROCm serving for each model in the supported model set on the
  dedicated AMD Instinct hardware, covering the serving configurations the
  platform supports for the CUDA runtime.
- Collect functional results (correctness, failures, workarounds) and
  performance measurements per model.
- Produce a validation report stating, per model: functional parity outcome,
  performance parity data, and the overall go/no-go scope for productization —
  the explicit list of models cleared for productization.
- Record which upstream ROCm runtime image versions were validated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists that covers every model in the supported model
  set, with a per-model functional pass/fail outcome and performance
  measurements obtained on AMD Instinct hardware.
- The report's performance data is comparable against the CUDA baseline for
  the same model set, so parity can be assessed per model.
- The report states the go/no-go scope for productization as an explicit list
  of cleared models (possibly empty, in the no-go case).
- The report records the upstream ROCm runtime image versions and hardware
  configuration used, so results are reproducible.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. This
  epic delivers that campaign and its report in full.

## Risks

- Hardware access (procurement or partner-lab) is unresolved and externally
  controlled; it gates campaign execution but is not a condition the campaign's
  deliverable produces, so it is tracked here rather than as an acceptance
  criterion.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; the campaign validates the versions available at execution time.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic delivers a supported, productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the
models the validation campaign clears. Today the platform ships only CUDA
(NVIDIA) builds of its serving runtimes; ROCm builds exist upstream but are not
shipped or supported. This epic turns the validated ROCm capability into a
productized runtime image with its serving-runtime packaging, scoped to the
model list produced by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: it
productizes exactly the models the campaign clears — a partial clear rewrites
the scope to that subset, and a full no-go removes the work entirely.

## Scope

- Build and release the vLLM ROCm runtime image from the midstream vLLM repo,
  pinned to the upstream ROCm base image version validated by the campaign.
- Provide the serving-runtime packaging (ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime)
  that deploys the ROCm vLLM runtime under KServe InferenceServices, aligned
  with how the CUDA vLLM runtime is packaged today.
- Limit the supported/declared model scope to the models cleared by the
  validation campaign.
- Verify KServe InferenceService deployments using the ROCm serving runtime
  (raw deployment mode) — KServe itself requires no code changes for ROCm
  (passive component), so this verification is an acceptance criterion here
  rather than separate work.
- Declare the support status and supported model list for the productized
  runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vLLM ROCm runtime image builds green in the component's existing build
  pipeline and is released for the target platform version.
- The released image is pinned to the validated upstream ROCm base image
  version, recorded in the release metadata.
- Serving of every model on the campaign's cleared list completes successfully
  via a KServe InferenceService using the ROCm serving runtime in raw
  deployment mode.
- The supported model list and support status are declared for the productized
  runtime.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears. This epic delivers the productized
  runtime, its packaging, and its support declaration; the KServe verification
  (passive-component validation, same owning team) is bundled as an acceptance
  criterion above.

## Risks

- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities and may not align with our release trains — a schedule risk on
  the productization timeline, mitigated by pinning the validated image
  version.
- Scope is parametric on the validation campaign's cleared-model list; a
  reduced or empty outcome rewrites or removes this epic's scope.

# PyTorch ROCm training support for single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJob workloads

## Description

This epic delivers PyTorch training support on AMD Instinct accelerators
(ROCm) for the Training Operator: platform-supported PyTorchJobs running
single- and multi-GPU training on AMD GPU nodes, using a supported PyTorch
ROCm training image. Today accelerated training in the platform is validated
on NVIDIA GPUs only; this epic extends the PyTorchJob path to ROCm.

## Scope

- Provide a supported PyTorch ROCm training image (single- and multi-GPU) for
  platform training workloads, built and released alongside the platform.
- Enable PyTorchJob workloads to target AMD GPU nodes exposed through the
  AMD device plugin (`amd.com/gpu` resource), including the job spec and
  scheduling aspects needed for ROCm workers.
- Validate single-GPU and multi-GPU PyTorchJob training runs on AMD Instinct
  nodes, including admission through the platform's workload queueing, which
  provides the `amd.com/gpu` quota handling configured by the Distributed
  Workloads stack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using the supported PyTorch ROCm training image
  completes a training run on AMD Instinct nodes.
- A multi-GPU PyTorchJob using the supported PyTorch ROCm training image
  completes distributed training across multiple AMD GPUs (single node and/or
  multi-node as supported).
- Shared end-to-end integration checkpoint (with the quota/admission slice
  delivered by the same team in the Distributed Workloads stack, which owns the
  quota/admission acceptance criteria): PyTorchJob workloads requesting
  `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through the platform's workload queueing and run
  on AMD GPU nodes.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. This
  epic delivers the PyTorchJob/ROCm training slice (job support, training
  image, and execution validation); the quota-handling slice is delivered by
  the Kueue-side work in the Distributed Workloads stack — the two slices are
  separate components and run in parallel, with the end-to-end admission flow
  integration-tested by this same owning team.

## Risks

- Validation requires dedicated AMD Instinct hardware; access (procurement or
  partner-lab) is unresolved and externally controlled — an availability
  precondition tracked here rather than as an acceptance criterion.
- Upstream PyTorch ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities and may constrain which versions can be supported per release.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic delivers `amd.com/gpu` quota and admission handling in the
Distributed Workloads stack (Kueue) so that ROCm training and serving
workloads requesting AMD GPUs are queued, admitted, and accounted correctly.
Kueue's existing quota model (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue with all-or-nothing
admission) currently governs NVIDIA GPU resources; this epic extends the
quota/admission configuration to AMD GPU resources.

## Scope

- Define and ship the Kueue resource flavor and quota configuration for AMD
  GPU nodes (`amd.com/gpu` resources) — ClusterQueue/LocalQueue setup for
  AMD-GPU node pools.
- Ensure quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) admission semantics work
  for workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu`, including multi-GPU and multi-pod
  job topologies used by distributed training.
- Validate admission of single- and multi-GPU ROCm jobs through the queueing
  layer with correct quota accounting, in coordination with the PyTorchJob
  ROCm training support delivered by the same team in the Training Operator.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted through Kueue with correct
  quota accounting against the configured ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quotas.
- Multi-GPU job topologies requesting multiple `amd.com/gpu` resources are
  admitted all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady gang semantics), so partially
  admitted ROCm jobs do not consume quota.
- Quota exhaustion for `amd.com/gpu` results in pending (not failed)
  workloads, consistent with the behavior for existing GPU resources.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. This
  epic delivers the quota/admission slice of that requirement; the
  PyTorchJob/ROCm job-support slice is delivered by the Training Operator
  work — separate component and repo, running in parallel, with the
  end-to-end flow integration-tested by this same owning team.

## Risks

- Validation requires dedicated AMD Instinct hardware; access (procurement or
  partner-lab) is unresolved and externally controlled — an availability
  precondition tracked here rather than as an acceptance criterion.

# Document AMD GPU (ROCm) supported hardware, drivers, and validated models

## Description

This epic delivers the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm)
enablement: what AMD hardware is supported, which driver prerequisites must be
installed, and which models are validated for the ROCm serving runtime. It is
authored after the implementation work so the content describes what was
actually built and validated.

## Scope

Content outline (to be authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- **Supported AMD hardware**: the supported AMD Instinct accelerators and node
  requirements for serving and training.
- **Driver prerequisites**: the ROCm driver stack and device plugin
  prerequisites (`amd.com/gpu` resource exposure) for AMD GPU nodes.
- **Validated model list**: the models cleared by the validation campaign and
  supported by the productized vLLM ROCm serving runtime.
- **Serving on ROCm**: using the productized ROCm serving runtime under KServe
  InferenceServices.
- **Training on ROCm**: running single- and multi-GPU PyTorch training jobs
  on AMD GPUs, admitted through the platform's workload queueing with
  `amd.com/gpu` quota handling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation topics state the supported AMD hardware, the driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list, matching the validation
  campaign results and the productized runtime's declared support scope.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented serving runtime
  and training support (reviewed by the owning engineering teams) and any
  discrepancies found in review are resolved.
- The documented model list matches the productized runtime's supported model
  list exactly — no undocumented supported models and no documented
  unsupported models.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list. This epic delivers that
  documentation in full; it also covers the training-support usage that the
  same strategy delivers.

## Notes

- Epic priority is P1, derived from the strategy's overall priority
  (Major) per the docs-authoring priority exception, not from the HLR's P2
  label.
- The docs owner team is assumed (the strategy provides no Impacted Teams
  table); confirm before submission.
